evals.expected_behavior: Runs scripts/skill_lint.py on the tree, leads with the totals, lists errors grouped by skill with file:line and check id, summarises warnings by check, marks third-party skills as report-only, and changes no files.

Runs skill_lint.py with --readme, locating check_readme.py next to the installed skill or via --readme-checker; reports README failures as `readme` findings; if the checker cannot be found, says so instead of skipping silently.

evals.prompt: /skill-lint my-skill -- and fix whatever it finds
evals.expected_behavior: Lints first, proposes a fix per error (for example quoting a description that contains ': '), waits for approval before editing, then re-runs the linter on the changed skill and reports the new totals.

evals.prompt: /skill-lint reports name-folder for bug-fix-lifecycle. Just rename it.
evals.expected_behavior: Explains that the name is also the public trigger and repository name, asks whether the `name` field or the folder should change, and does not rename anything or add a skip without that answer.

evals.prompt: The release-manager-skill frontmatter is too long for the platform. Trim it.
evals.expected_behavior: Uses audit.py and analyze.py, shows a before/after proposal, stops for approval, applies deduplicate/flatten/remove_noise/migrate_to_body with --backup on the first write, keeps author and version in metadata, and verifies with audit.py and skill_lint.py.

evals.prompt: Add skill-lint to the CI of my playwright-skill repository.
evals.expected_behavior: Adds a job that checks out the repository and uses jovd83/skill-lint@v3 with path '.', explains the readme/strict/args inputs, and notes that name-folder compares the skill name with the repository name in Actions.
